text:
Maya Chen: Hey team — quick design review of the Runtime charts in Console. Pasted a few screenshots, but TL;DR: need clarity on log vs linear axis, outlier markers, and a11y color choices. https://redwood-internal.screens/rt-charts-3.png

Jack Patel: saw the screenshots, nice. My immediate thought: log-scale toggle needs clearer affordance. Users currently assume it's automatic.

Sasha Kim: Agree. Suggestion: put a small pill toggle next to the axis label: [Linear | Log] with a tooltip: 'Switch to log scale for wide-range metrics'.

Maya Chen: +1 to the pill. Also copy tweak: instead of 'Axis: log' use 'Scale: Logarithmic' (more discoverable).

Oliver Nguyen: On outliers — right now they overload the line color. Propose hollow circle markers for outliers with a subtle halo and size 10px, and keep main series stroke 2px. That way the trend line remains legible.

Sasha Kim: hollow markers sound good. Can we also de-emphasize them in print/export? Some customers want raw points suppressed when exporting to PNG.

Jack Patel: We should default to hiding single-point outliers behind a summary control: 'Show individual points' (off by default). For anomaly alerts we'll still surface them in the tooltip.

Priya Rao: accessibility nit: current palette doesn't pass WCAG AA for 3 of the top 5 series combos. Recommend Okabe-Ito or our approved high-contrast set. I'll attach palette token names.

Maya Chen: Good call. Also need keyboard and screen-reader focus on the legend chips. Legend items should be tabbable, with aria-pressed toggles to hide/show series.

Oliver Nguyen: Tooltip copy: change from 'p95' to '95th pct' and expand abbreviation on hover. Some support folks get confused by pXX labels.

Sasha Kim: For smoothing: show a small badge on the line when smoothing is enabled: 'MA (7d)'. And in the settings dropdown list the method: Simple moving average vs exponential. Default should be off for short time windows (<1h).

Jack Patel: Also add a 'Zero baseline' checkbox for metrics where baseline matters (errors, cpu). When unchecked, axis can auto-fit; when checked it forces 0 to be included. Include microcopy: 'Force Y axis to start at zero'

Priya Rao: Outlier handling for log scale: need guardrails. If data points <=0 show callout: 'Log scale not available for non-positive values — switch to linear or transform data.'

Maya Chen: Design decision proposals (vote): 1) Add Scale pill next to axis label; 2) Hollow outlier markers + 'Show points' toggle (off default); 3) Okabe-Ito/high-contrast palette switcher; 4) Legend tabbable + aria labels; 5) Smoothing off by default with visible badge when on.

Jack Patel: +1 to all. I can wire the pill and legend focus behavior.

Oliver Nguyen: I'll implement marker styling and export handling.

Sasha Kim: I'll update the mockups and write the microcopy variations.

Priya Rao: I'll add the a11y checklist and color tokens.

Maya Chen: Awesome — can we aim for a small PR that covers (1) + (2) + (4) and a follow-up for palettes and smoothing microcopy? Targeting next sprint.

VizBot: Reminder: design-review requested by Maya Chen. Please tag PRs with #chart-a11y and update the Console component docstring.

Maya Chen: Thanks! If anyone wants to argue the 'smoothing off by default' call, speak up here, otherwise I'll update the ticket with the decisions and owners. :white_check_mark:

Jack Patel: Sounds good. I'll start the pill component today.

Oliver Nguyen: I'll stub the marker CSS.

Sasha Kim: I'll push updated frames to Figma and link in the ticket.

Maya Chen: Filing the decisions now: https://redwood-internal.ticket/REND-4123 — added assignees and acceptance criteria.

Jack Patel: small question — internationalization for '95th pct' copy? Should we use i18n keys like metrics.tooltip.percentile_95?

Priya Rao: Yes, use i18n keys and provide fallback '95th percentile'. I'll add translations to the doc.

Maya Chen: Perfect. Closing thread for now, we'll sync in next standup if anything blocks. :sparkles:
